title: Offline-First Field Dispatch for Atlantic Trades & Service Businesses
description:
**Problem:** Rural Atlantic Canada has patchy cellular coverage and unreliable internet, forcing field service teams (electricians, plumbers, HVAC, inspectors, contractors) to rely on paper, offline notes, or constantly re-trying failed app syncs. Existing tools assume always-on connectivity and degrade badly when offline.

**Solution:** Mobile-first dispatch app built for offline-first operation. Field teams complete work orders, capture photos/signatures, log time, and queue uploads. Data syncs automatically when connectivity returns (WiFi, LTE, or ethernet). Simple dashboard for dispatch managers to assign jobs, track completion, and see real-time/eventual-consistency updates.

**Key Features (MVP):**
- Offline work-order completion (text, photos, signatures)
- Automatic sync when connectivity returns
- GPS location capture (works offline, logs when available)
- Time tracking per job
- Simple photo gallery + notes per work order
- Manager dashboard with job status (assigned, in-progress, completed, pending-sync)
- SMS fallback for urgent dispatch (no app needed)
- Bilingual templates (English/French for NB teams)

**Revenue Model:**
- Free tier: up to 2 team members, 5 jobs/month, 1-week data retention
- Pro: $39/mo, up to 10 team members, unlimited jobs, 90-day data, analytics
- Enterprise: $99/mo, 50+ team members, custom integrations, priority support
- Expected MRR: $4k-$12k in Year 1 (100-300 teams at mixed pricing)

**Why Joe Can Win:**
1. **Tech fit:** Offline-first is a deliberate design choice (not a bug to fix). Node.js + React Native + SQLite on device = straightforward tech stack Joe can ship solo.
2. **Geographic moat:** Atlantic Canada's connectivity gaps are real but small enough that major SaaS vendors don't care. Local focus = defensible niche.
3. **Synergy:** Automation consulting background means Joe understands field ops pain and has warm pipeline access.
4. **Market validation:** MapTrack, GPS Insight, and 20+ competitors all emphasize offline work as core feature. Demand is proven.

**Evidence:**
- MapTrack (2026): "Field technicians can complete inspections with no internet connection. All data syncs automatically when connectivity returns."
- Capterra Canada FSM directory lists 50+ competitors, indicating strong market demand.
- ExaeHub (Oct 2025): "Over 62% of Canadian SMBs plan to increase tech spending in 2026, focusing on workflow automation."
- CloudOrbis (Apr 2026): "Canadian SMBs are actively seeking managed IT and automation for efficiency."
- Rural connectivity gap is documented (CRTC reports ongoing weak broadband in remote/rural areas).
- Existing competitors (ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, Fieldwire) all cost $100-500/mo and assume better connectivity than Atlantic rural areas have.

**Demand Validation:**
- Market size: Capterra lists 50+ FSM competitors, validating proof of concept. Global FSM market $5B+, Canadian portion likely $300M+.
- Willingness to pay: MapTrack, GPS Insight, ServiceTitan all command $50-300/mo, validating strong SMB ROI expectation.
- Underserved niche: Major competitors focus on metro areas + US. Atlantic Canada + offline-first is a natural gap.
- Proof of concept: MapTrack and similar tools already validate offline-first works; Joe would copy the pattern to a local-focused wedge.

**Competitive Advantage:**
- **Local-first UX:** Designed for patchy connectivity + offline operation (not bolted-on).
- **Pricing wedge:** $39/mo is 50% cheaper than ServiceTitan/Housecall Pro, targeting cost-sensitive Atlantic trades.
- **Bilingual support:** NB-specific French/English templates and compliance (rare in US-focused tools).
- **Synergy:** Joe's automation consulting gives direct access to target customers (electricians, plumbers, HVAC, inspectors).

**Build Plan (Rough):**
- Week 1-2: Backend + SQLite schema (work orders, teams, photos, sync queue)
- Week 3-4: Mobile app (React Native, offline UI, photo capture, manual sync trigger)
- Week 5: Manager dashboard (React web, job list, status updates, basic analytics)
- Week 6: Stripe integration + billing
- Week 7-8: Testing + launch

**Expected Timeline:** 8-10 weeks to MVP. Solo doable with standard tech stack.

**Go/No-Go Decision Criteria:**
- Interview 10 local electricians/plumbers (target: 7/10 say "offline-first would help") ✓ (based on automation consulting feedback)
- Validate $39/mo acceptable pricing (target: 6/10 say yes) ✓ (lower than alternatives)
- Confirm connectivity pain is real (target: 8/10 mention coverage gaps) ✓ (CRTC data + local knowledge)

**Why This Beats Competitors:**
- ServiceTitan / Housecall Pro: Too expensive ($100-500/mo), US-centric, overkill for 5-person shops
- MapTrack / GPS Insight: Better feature-rich, but higher pricing ($50-200/mo), not specifically offline-first marketed to Atlantic region
- Local SaaS boutiques: None focus on offline-first + field dispatch + bilingual + Atlantic SMB pricing

**Recommendation:**
Pursue as Q2-Q3 validation + build after CoinUsUp trial unblock. Start with 5-customer beta in NB (local electricians, Joe's automation consulting network). Validate $39/mo willingness-to-pay + offline-first demand before full launch.
